dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the artifact: it collects Google Maps business listing data such as names, addresses, phone numbers, websites, ratings, and review counts through BrowserAct. That scraping and lead-generation capability can have privacy, compliance, and terms-of-service implications, but it is not hidden or purpose-mismatched.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill encourages proactive use across many business-research scenarios and allows one automatic retry after non-auth failures. This is broad, but visible, bounded, and aligned with the advertised Google Maps scraping workflow.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains a SKILL.md file and one Python helper script. I found no install hooks, package installation behavior, obfuscation, self-modification, or startup registration.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires Python and BROWSERACT_API_KEY, then sends the API key plus user-provided keywords, language, and country to BrowserAct API endpoints. This network and credential use is expected for the integration and declared in the skill metadata and setup instructions, though users should understand the external data flow.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The script does not write local files, read broad local data, spawn background services, request elevated privileges, or persist state locally; it starts and polls a BrowserAct task and prints returned results.

dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The artifact does use an environment API key and outbound BrowserAct calls, but the API key requirement is declared and the code uses it only as a Bearer token for BrowserAct workflow endpoints.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad proactive trigger language is real and could cause overuse, but it is visible in the description and tied to the stated business-data scraping purpose rather than hidden automation.
[SQP-2] expected: The skill collects business contact details and sends search parameters to BrowserAct; this data flow is inferable from the BrowserAct API usage and script, but users would benefit from a clearer plain-language notice before broad lead-generation runs.
[VirusTotal] expected: VirusTotal telemetry was clean and consistent with the artifact review, but it was not used as the sole basis for the verdict.
[static-scan] expected: Static scan reported no findings, and direct review found no command execution, credential harvesting, destructive behavior, persistence, or unrelated filesystem access.
llm.guidance: Install this only if you intend to use BrowserAct for Google Maps data collection. Keep the BrowserAct API key in environment configuration rather than pasting it into chat, confirm before broad or recurring lead-generation searches, and consider privacy, compliance, and site terms before collecting phone numbers or other business contact data.
llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed BrowserAct Google Maps business-data scraper, with the main caution that searches and the API key are sent to BrowserAct.
